decided: emit.Exporter's post-Shutdown contract is a disjunction: after Shutdown returns, a call to ExportMetrics/ExportEvents on a capable signal must either be refused (return a non-nil error and deliver nothing) or remain genuinely functional (return nil and demonstrably deliver to the backend). What no implementation may do is accept a post-Shutdown batch and silently absorb it. Push-transport exporters whose delivery depends on a flush that has already happened (otlp, cloudwatch, gcp) must take the refuse branch; a pull-collected exporter (prometheus) may keep a no-op Shutdown and stay functional. The conformance suite enforces the disjunction behaviorally — export after Shutdown, then require error-and-nothing-delivered or nil-and-everything-delivered — with no new Caps field.
why: The defect class that motivated this (workspace-9h1) is silent post-Shutdown absorption: cloudwatch and gcp today accept post-Shutdown writes into a bufio.Writer that nothing will ever flush again, which is invisible loss of outcome data — exactly what the review charter's fail-open item forbids. But mandating 'terminal' universally would break prometheus, whose no-op Shutdown is deliberate and correct for a scrape transport (unregistering would delete series before a final scrape, and post-Shutdown registry updates lose nothing). The disjunction bans the only genuinely defective behavior while leaving both legitimate designs intact, and it is checkable from the outside via the existing Backend counting interface, so the contract is enforced rather than documented.
cost_if_wrong: If too loose: an adapter author reads the contract, ships an exporter that silently drops post-Shutdown outcome events, and money vanishes from the record with no counter incremented — the highest-severity class in this library. If too strict: scrape-based exporters are forced to guard or unregister, breaking final-scrape correctness and inventing failure modes for a transport that has none.
alternatives: Shutdown terminal for all implementations (post-Shutdown Export always errors): rejected — breaks prometheus's deliberate no-op Shutdown, which loses nothing and is correct for pull collection.

Shutdown flush-only for all (Export must keep working after): rejected — for push transports this requires every Export to self-flush or reintroduces the silent-absorption window; contradicts otlp's terminal design fixed in workspace-9h1.

Declare the mode in emit.Caps (e.g. TerminalShutdown bool): rejected — a declared bit can lie where behavior cannot; Caps mirrors query.Caps and widening both is a larger contract change than this needs, and the behavioral disjunction is testable without it.
scope: emit.Exporter doc contract (emit/emit.go); testkit/conformance (two new invariants + suite self-tests); adapters/export/cloudwatch and adapters/export/gcp gain post-Shutdown guards mirroring otlp's ErrShutdown pattern; adapters/export/otlp and adapters/export/prometheus unchanged. otlp's second-Shutdown return value is out of scope (workspace-shl).
